1.why: act - A/B/C each assert a flat fact about the panels; D alone performs the measured reinterpretation ('better evidence of a convention than of the vessels'), which is the act a main-idea stem in this bank almost always rewards.

2.why: knowledge - pine is a prodigious wind-pollen producer, so its grains over-represent its standing abundance and a modest loss of trees reads as a disproportionate fall; A and D share the 'out of proportion' shape but only A stays inside the pollen record the other options describe.

3.why: knowledge - burrow aeration of waterlogged/anoxic soil is the canonical mechanism; C names a stressor (salt) running the wrong way and D (extra light at a hole in the soil) is not a real mechanism.

4.why: shape - A and C are exact mirror swaps of the same four cells, so one is false; D independently corroborates A's variety 1 = 12 at Site A, which kills C.

5.why: none - A and B are identical but for the 1-month figure (34 vs 30) and nothing outside the table discriminates; C changes the endpoint the lead-in names and D's 44 is uncorroborated by the three options that agree on 6 points at 10 minutes.

6.why: shape - B gives Layer 1 a total of 96 and Layer 4 a total of 86, so D's '58 of the 86 in Layer 1' misassigns a total and is false; between A and C over the same cells, 150/240 is the exaggerated misread of a column total.

7.why: knowledge - a thicket throwing up new stems each spring is a clonal shrub, and the stems are ramets of the same individuals; C and D both require seedling recruitment under grazing, which is the standard thing such thickets do NOT do.

8.why: act - only A ties the appearance of the new rim to households in demonstrable contact with the upstream village; B establishes priority only, D establishes speed only, C is irrelevant quality.

9.why: none - A, B and C are all legal readings of a cold-plus-cross-feeding setup; I took C because a bacterium that vanishes only in company points to competition for the shared sugar rather than to cold acting on it directly.

10.why: act - C and D blame oversight or linguistic impossibility; A alone performs the knowing-and-declining reading that a main-idea stem about two divergent treaty texts is built to reward.

11.why: shape - A and B share '23 minutes longer than the barbet' (so that comparison is real) and then contradict each other on distance, but nothing visible decides between decoupling (A) and concordance (B); C and D also run decoupling, so the direction is 3-1 and I followed the corroborated comparator.

12.why: direction - the proposal needs a route and a source direction; only D supplies a signature match plus an upriver age gradient. B is a non-match, C argues against import, A dates the hull not the cargo.

13.why: act - the divergence after a dam needs an explanation that leaves the proxy intact; C alone reinterprets what the rings record, while D discards the reconstruction and B misstates what a dam does to total water.

14.why: act - B is the standard split verdict (distant material, local manufacture) that a main-idea stem about recovered ivory pieces is assembled from; A inverts it, C and D deny local working.

15.why: act - C is the only manipulation that removes the proposed cue and reports failure; A removes the destination, B is a timing correlation, D tests conspecific trails instead of the snail's own.

16.why: shape - A and D agree that 28 percent remained at 20 m from 0.1 m, so that cell is real and B/C (which contradict each other over the 5 m row) are the mutated pair; between A and D I took the larger contrast with the highest source, which is a coin flip.

17.why: none - A, B and D all hedge the observation and any of the three fits a plausible claim about journal evidence; I took D because it pairs a countable record with its own stated limit, which is what a study using such journals as data would illustrate.

18.why: act - B and C describe mechanical revision facts; D performs the 'less X than Y' reinterpretation and subsumes A's narrower claim about the self-correcting manner.

19.why: knowledge - deceptive pollination is limited by pollinator learning and avoidance; D asserts the opposite of the known dynamic, C denies the deception the text has set up, A invents a pollen cost deceit does not carry.

20.why: act - only D reproduces the brittleness experimentally from a process step; A supports the rival compositional explanation, B and C are circumstance with no link to the outcome.

21.why: shape - B and C are mirror swaps of the 400 m and 800 m counts, and A independently corroborates 31 at 400 m, so B falls; the surviving reading is the mid-elevation peak.

22.why: act - A, B and C each state one effect or one mechanism; D alone states the split outcome (one species favored, two displaced) that a main-idea stem about a relit road wants.

23.why: act - the proposal is that the orchid exploits an association the moths already have with the shrub, and only C manipulates rearing history to test that association; D and A are co-occurrence, B tests innate attraction.

24.why: act - A and B contradict each other over the same recordings, and a 'second of two accounts' stem is built to reframe the recordings as registering a change already made rather than as the moment of it (C, D).

cross_item_rule.rule: On every non-quantitative stem, sort the options by rhetorical act and take the one whose act matches the stem, ignoring content. Main-idea stems (1, 10, 14, 18, 22) key to the single option that performs a measured reinterpretation or a split verdict while the other three assert flat single facts - fired 5 times, 5 picks. Support/finding stems (8, 12, 15, 20, 23) key to the single option that manipulates or directly links the proposed mechanism while the others supply circumstance, priority or a rival explanation - fired 5 times, 5 picks. A second rule, canonical biology, decided 3 (burrow aeration), 7 (clonal ramets) and 19 (learned avoidance limits deceptive pollination) with no passage at all - 3 items, and these are the author's two flagged items plus one more.

constraining_pairs.note: No cross-ITEM constraint exists - the 24 items share no quantity. Every constraint found is between OPTIONS WITHIN one quantitative item, and this is the finding that matters for the author's claim: the rebuild made all four options run the lead-in's direction, but it left the numbers mutually inconsistent, so options corroborate and refute each other with the figure still covered.

pairs.conflict: exact mirror swap of variety 1 and variety 2 at Sites A and B (12/38/15 vs 40/15/38); one must be false, and D's independent 'variety 1 = 12 at Site A' breaks the tie against C.

same two cells, 1-month advantage 34 vs 30; one is false. D's 44 for the same cell makes three incompatible values. This is the only quantitative item where the conflict does NOT resolve - it is the model for how the others should have been built.
Layer 1's scored total is 96 in B and 86 in D (86 is B's Layer 4 total); D misassigns a denominator and is false without the table. Separately A vs C put 47 and 150 in the same numerator cell.

both fix retention at 23 minutes longer than the barbet, then disagree on distance (about the same vs more than three times as far); the shared clause is evidence the comparison is real, the disagreement leaves one of them false.
same 5 m row read two ways (71/96 vs 64/88); one is false. A and D agreeing on 28 percent at 20 m from 0.1 m marks that cell as the true one and pushes the key into the A/D pair.
mirror swap of the 400 m and 800 m counts (44 then 22 vs 31 then 44); A's '31 at 400 m' corroborates C's first value and eliminates B.

constraining_pairs.verdict_on_author_claim: The direction rebuild held - on all six quantitative items every option runs the direction the lead-in names, and none was answerable by direction alone. But five of the six leaked a different way: distractors were built by mutating the key's cells, so options quote each other's numbers and a majority vote across options reconstructs part of the hidden table. Item 5 is the only one of the six that is genuinely undecidable blind.
